html.body: Author: Marcio Acencio, Luxembourg Centre for Systens Biomedicine, University of Luxembourg Description: Set of pathways encompassing the replication cycle of SARS-CoV-2: attachment, entry, translation, transcription, replication, assembly and release.

Name: cytoplasm
All of the contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

Name: virion
The complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle. Any constituent part of a virion, a complete fully infectious extracellular virus particle.

Name: azurophil granule
Primary lysosomal granule readily stainable with a Romanowsky stain.

Name: extracellular region
The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

Name: viral nucleocapsid
The complete protein-nucleic acid complex that is the packaged form of the genome in a virus particle.

Name: cell surface
The external part of the cell wall and/or plasma membrane.

Name: neutrophil activation Charge: 0
The change in morphology and behavior of a neutrophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

Name: symbiont entry into host cell Charge: 0
The process by which a symbiont breaches the plasma membrane or cell envelope and enters the host cell. The process ends when the symbiont or its genome is released into the host cell.
